title: Sustainability-Aware Knowledge Graph Completion for Supply Chain Decision Support: code, enriched data and full experimental results
description:
Complete replication package for the manuscript Sustainability-Aware Knowledge Graph Completion for Supply Chain Decision Support: Multi-Objective Training, Externally Grounded Risk and Disruption-Level Evaluation, submitted to Sustainability (MDPI).

The package contains the full experimental pipeline that rebuilds and extends the evaluation of Peeris, Baryannis and Papadakis (2026), Sustainability 18(6):2825, doi:10.3390/su18062825.

This version adds the post-hoc sustainability-filtering baseline (recommend_posthoc_filter in src/suschain/decision_eval/disruption_simulation.py, run via scripts/20_disruption_multiseed.py), which re-ranks the plain model's own top-50 candidates by risk before keeping the top 5, the mechanism Peeris et al. describe in their Section 3.3 but do not implement or evaluate. It also fixes overlapping node labels in the predicted-links figures.

Contents

  • src/suschain/ - library: dataset loaders, heterogeneous graph builders, GraphSAGE/GAT/RGCN encoders, dot-product/bilinear/MLP decoders, non-learned heuristics, PyKEEN knowledge-graph-embedding wrappers, multi-objective sustainability-aware training, post-hoc risk-filtering re-ranking, ranking and significance-testing utilities, type-restricted KGE ranking and both GAT attention variants (GATv2 and the original GAT).
  • scripts/ - numbered, runnable pipeline reproducing every table and figure in the manuscript, from descriptive statistics through the benchmark, node classification, the lambda sweep, the disruption simulation (including the post-hoc filtering baseline), the inductive evaluation, the type-aware KGE re-evaluation and the GATv2-versus-GAT sensitivity experiment.
  • results/metrics/ - one JSON per experiment, each recording configuration, random seed and full metric set. Every number reported in the manuscript traces to a file here.
  • results/tables/ - the manuscript tables as CSV.
  • data/raw/ - the two source datasets exactly as used: LODHalal and AnonNet.
  • data/processed/ - the enriched, real-sustainability-grounded label sets derived in the paper.
  • data/external/ - the Our World in Data CO2 reference table used for the AnonNet carbon-intensity grounding.
  • tests/ - unit tests covering splitting, ranking and the sustainability enrichment.

Not included: the Open Food Facts product dump (1.2 GB) and the derived sentence-transformer embedding cache. Both are third-party or regenerable; scripts/08_offmatch_lodhalal.py downloads and rebuilds them.

Environment: Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.5.1, PyTorch Geometric 2.6.1, CUDA 12.4. Pinned in requirements.txt.
